subject: Archaeology
title: The Pantheon: Engineering Perfection
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Pantheon: Engineering Perfection.

hook.text: The Pantheon's dome is still the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome — after nearly 2,000 years.

buildup.text: Hadrian rebuilt the Pantheon around 125 CE. Its dome spans 142 feet and has a 27-foot hole at the top called the oculus.

discovery.text: The concrete gets lighter toward the top. Builders mixed in pumice near the crown to reduce weight — brilliant.

twist.text: Rain enters through the oculus and drains through nearly invisible floor holes.

climax.text: It survived because it was converted into a church in 609 CE. Pagan temples that were not reused were stripped for materials.

punchline.text: Christianity saved a pagan temple by changing its name, not its dome.

quiz.question: Why has the Pantheon survived nearly 2,000 years?
options: It was buried underground and rediscovered in the Renaissance
It was converted into a church in 609 CE, protecting it from demolition
Earthquakes never affected the area where it was built

details.summary: The Pantheon in Rome, rebuilt by Hadrian around 126 CE, contains the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome — 43 meters across with an open oculus at its center. Nearly two thousand years old, it remains structurally perfect and continues to function as a building today.
details.whyItMatters: The Pantheon is the most perfectly preserved ancient building and proof that Roman engineering rivaled or exceeded modern capabilities in some respects. Its dome was unsurpassed in size for over 1,300 years.
takeaways: The Pantheon has the largest unreinforced concrete dome ever built
The dome is 43 meters across with an open oculus at the top
It has survived nearly 2,000 years in continuous use

faq.question: How does the Pantheon's dome stay up without reinforcement?
faq.answer: Roman engineers varied the concrete's density — heavier aggregate at the base, lighter pumice near the top — and used coffered panels to reduce weight. The dome's perfect hemispherical geometry distributes stress evenly, and the oculus removes the heaviest section at the apex.

faq.question: What happens when it rains through the oculus?
faq.answer: Rain does fall through the 9-meter-wide opening, but the slightly concave floor has drain holes that channel water away. The volume of rain entering is relatively small, and the building's thermal dynamics create upward air currents that partially deflect lighter rainfall.
